subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.
reasoning:
Since this is a static vehicle rather than a creature, I don't need a joint hierarchy—I can keep the geometry simple in the root. I'm planning a six-wheeled carrier roughly 9 meters long facing +Z, with wheels sized at 0.7 radius and 0.5 width.

I'm sketching the hull chassis, a front cab, and a rear turret-mounted railgun with twin barrels, rails, coil rings, and a muzzle facing forward, plus four deployed hydraulic stabilizer legs with ground-touching pads, making sure wheels and pads both sit flush at ground level. For texturing I'll use SVG decals—hazard stripes, an emblem, warning labels, cab windows, and a unit number—built from the SDK's paint, mottle, noise, and stripe utilities along with a glow kit, assembling parts as simple boxes and cylinders oriented with directional vectors rather than any bone structure.

Now I'm working out wheel placement: six wheels across three axles along the hull, dark tire cylinders with lighter hub rims and lug nuts, positioned so the rear stays heavy enough to support the railgun's weight. I'm also figuring out where the cab sits versus the turret so the barrel can tilt upward slightly and extend forward over the cab with proper clearance.

Still building rail geometry and coil rings...

Still working out the extrusion geometry...

Now I'm positioning the windshield decal plane along the slanted cab surface, computing its normal and midpoint, then adding side window planes with their own placement and simple textures.

Next I'm planning the front details: glowing headlight boxes, grille texture, bumper, tow hooks, cab antennas, and an amber light bar on the roof. Then I'm shifting to the rear, sketching the gun carriage deck height and hull profile points to define the chassis shape toward the back.

For the turret, I'm positioning it on the deck with a ring cylinder base, a boxy turret body, trunnion pivot height for the barrel, and side cheek plates to hold the barrel assembly in place.

I'm computing the barrel's geometry with a slight upward pitch angle, tracing where it exits above the cab, and setting up the lateral rail boxes that flank the barrel for support.

Now I'm placing coil rings along the barrel at intervals, giving each a dark steel band plus a thin glowing cyan ring, while checking the ring radius clears the rails underneath.

Realizing solid rings would hide the rails, I'm reconsidering the shape—maybe using open frame rings or a lathe-generated hollow cylindrical shell with an axis aligned to the barrel direction so the rails stay visible through them.

Now I'm adding a cyan glow strip running along the center between the rails, plus small glow bands on the lathed rings, then planning the breech block with bolts and a muzzle section with glow accents.

I'm placing capacitor banks on the turret sides as angled cylinders with connecting cable sweeps to the breech, then adding a rear generator box with vents and exhaust stacks, and working out positions for four stabilizer outrigger legs between the wheels.

Now I'm detailing the outrigger legs: horizontal beam arms extending from the hull sides, vertical hydraulic cylinders dropping to octagonal foot pads on the ground, plus diagonal brace rods and hazard-stripe decal textures on the arms.

I'm checking clearance between the outriggers and the wheels, making sure the arm height at y1.3 sits above each wheel's top radius without collision on both front and rear sides, and considering adding fenders over the wheels as simple boxes that stay clear of the arm geometry.

For wheel construction, I'm planning each wheel as a multi-sided tire cylinder with a separate steel rim disc, an orange hub cap, and six small lug nut cylinders arranged around the face, repeating this setup for all six wheels while keeping part count manageable.

Checking the rotation math confirms the radial angle placement works correctly. I need to adjust the tire radius down to .70 and shift the tread block positions so the lowest point stays just barely above zero rather than dipping below ground. Next I'm planning the hull paint job with an olive-drab camo pattern using a three-color mottled texture.

Working out the plane orientation math so decal text reads correctly on each hull side...

For the hull's side surfaces, I'm placing the roundel and number decals so they clear the wheel wells and fenders, settling on a position around z=0 for the roundel to avoid overlapping other side details.

For the fenders, I'm sizing each wheel's cover as a small box roughly .75 wide, .1 thick, 1.7 long, sitting just above the wheel top so it clears the tire but still connects to the hull edge for a solid attachment.

Now I'm adding under-hull axle beams running through the wheel positions, sized to fit beneath the hull bottom, plus differential bulge cylinders for mechanical detail. I'm also planning hull greebles like deck hatches, vents, side storage bins between wheel arches, and cargo tanks, then moving into shaping the turret body profile with a ring mount and extruded silhouette points.

Still writing turret geometry...

Now I'm adding the cheek support boxes above the turret and the breech housing block, then positioning trunnion cylinders where the barrel axis crosses the cheeks to figure out the elevation geometry.

Next I'm routing the hydraulic elevation rods from the turret base to the cradle underside on both sides, then turning to surface details—status light glows and capacitor drum cylinders mounted on the turret's rear deck.

Positioning the capacitor drums vertically behind the turret with glow bands, checking clearance against the barrel breech box, then sweeping black cable curves from the drum tops down to the breech using Catmull-Rom points.

Now I'm adding rear details: a tail ramp/bumper box with tow hook and red glowing tail lights, radiator vents with a textured plane, and exhaust stacks mounted behind the cab as dark capped cylinders. For the cab, I'm planning a roof hatch, light bar, antenna whips, and box-shaped mirrors.

Front end gets a grille texture plane, sloped hull pieces, and a hazard-striped bumper box using a diagonal yellow/black texture applied to all faces. I'm compiling a texture list -- hazard stripes, roundel, label decal, windshield, side window, grille, vents, warning triangle, and kill-mark rings for the turret side -- around eight textures total, plus a glowing effect for the gun barrel.

Now I'm sketching the remaining mechanical details: hydraulic sweep rods curving from hull to leg using a catmull spline, a turret ring cylinder, and a spike-based antenna. Then I move into actual code, setting up builder helper functions for boxes, cylinders, and decal planes, deciding that static models can skip joints since there's no articulation needed, and noting that colors and paints are passed as strings while a glow helper controls part intensity.

Writing SVG patterns...

Still designing car parts...

Still placing housing, piston, pad geometry...

Adding a hydraulic hose using a curved sweep from the hull to the housing, then double-checking clearance between the outrigger pad radius and the wheels at both the rear and front positions to make sure nothing overlaps.

Now I'm working through cab details: narrowing the cab extrusion width, adding a roof lightbar with amber glow caps, side mirrors with arm rods and glinting faces, and a roof armor plate sized to fit just above the cab profile without clipping.

For the front end, I'm placing warm-glow headlight boxes flanking a grille panel, with a hazard-textured bumper beneath spanning the hull's front face. On the rear, I'm adding vent planes and glowing tail lights to balance out the front lighting.

Now I'm working out the rear bumper and tow hook, then moving to deck details -- stowage boxes placed along the sides with camo texturing, and considering turret-side tanks or arms to add visual interest.

For the turret itself, I'm thinking about adding kill-mark decals on the sides and refining the muzzle with a shroud ring plus flush rail tips, working out the rail dimensions and cross-section emerging from the breech block.

Adding a central glow strip between the rails sized to fit the gap, deciding to skip insulator spacers, and sketching sensor elements like a small radar dome and antenna spikes on the turret roof.

Now I'm defining a helper function for positioning elements along the barrel axis with lateral and vertical offsets.

Still writing part placement code...

Still working out window placements and positions on the cab and hull...

Alright, I think I've got the geometry worked out well enough. Time to write the full output, keeping it around 350 lines.
